Exercise A

Arriving in the Northeast

Read the text about New York and Boston. Choose the correct word for each gap.

Before you read — optional, not marked
This is just to get you thinking — you can leave it empty and it does not count towards your score.
Reading Text

Exercise B

Comparative Adjectives: -er or more?

Short adjectives take -er (cold → colder). Longer adjectives take more (exciting → more exciting). Some are irregular: good → better, bad → worse.

Complete the Sentence

1. New York is than Boston.

2. The subway is than the bus.

3. Central Park is than I expected.

4. Winter in Boston is than winter in Miami.

5. This museum is interesting than the other one.

6. The weather today is than yesterday.

7. A ferry ticket is than a taxi ride.

8. The streets here are than the streets in my town.

Exercise C

Superlative Adjectives: the -est or the most?

Use the superlative when you compare one thing with all the others: the tallest building, the most famous museum.

Complete the Sentence

1. The Empire State Building is one of the buildings in New York.

2. That was the day of our whole trip.

3. Times Square is the place in the city.

4. Which is the museum in Boston?

5. This is the pizza I have ever eaten.

6. January is usually the month of the year here.

7. The subway is the way to travel across New York.

8. It was the holiday of my life.

Exercise D

Writing: My Town and New York

Compare your town with New York (6–8 sentences). Write about size, traffic, people, shops and free time. Use at least three comparatives and two superlatives.

Useful language
You can use these: bigger than smaller than quieter than more expensive than the best the most beautiful the busiest not as ... as
Your text
Aim for 6–8 sentences with three comparatives and two superlatives.
